title: Ops Telescope: Cost Experiments Repository & Rollout Schedule
creator: Lena Cho
description:
Goal: Create an experiment-first operational repository ("Ops Telescope") that standardizes how we run, observe, and roll out batching/caching/quantization experiments across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. The repository is a combination of: 1) an experiment manifest schema, 2) a telemetry tagging and dashboard convention, 3) an automated rollout cadence (canary -> ramp -> global) with quality/cost gates, and 4) a public changelog & lessons-learned registry so teams can reuse validated configurations.

Why: Our current signals and rollouts are fragmented across services and teams. That increases risk of quality regression and slows adoption of high-value cost knobs. Ops Telescope should reduce rollout friction, centralize SLI/SLOs for cost and quality, and create a predictable path from lab experiment to production-wide policy.

Core deliverables:
- Experiment manifest spec: fields for workload descriptors, traffic split, quant profile, batching parameters, cache TTLs, eval prompt set, success metrics, rollout plan, rollback criteria.
- Centralized experiment index: searchable registry with status, owner, links, and telemetry snapshots.
- Dashboard templates and alert rules: cost-per-1k-tokens SLI, latency P95, output-quality drift (eval-based), and rollout failure threshold.
- Canary orchestration: automated traffic shifting with pre/post check scripts & automatic rollback hooks.
- Playbook: runbook for experiment owners and infra for vetting, risk scoring, and stakeholder signoff.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment manifest schema published and versioned in the repo
Template dashboards created in Console and linked from the registry
Three internal pilot experiments run (one batching, one kv-cache, one quantization) with documented telemetry and lessons learned
Canary automation can route 5% -> 25% -> 100% with programmable gates and automated rollback
Open registry UI with search and filters for model, workload, owner, and status

risks: Quality regressions during quantization/batching that aren’t caught by current evals
Telemetry gaps for dedicated/private deployments due to restricted metrics export
Slow stakeholder signoff if experiment artifacts are not readable or lack clear criteria
Automation rollback hooks may conflict with existing routing policies in certain regions
